title: Build an RPN calculator in Rust — 3 turns
description: Three turns build an RPN (Reverse Polish Notation) calculator: turn 1 push/add/sub, turn 2 mul/div with zero-div error, turn 3 dup/swap.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `push(&mut self, value: f64)`, `pop(&mut self) -> Result<f64, CalcError>`, `add(&mut self) -> Result<(), CalcError>`, and `sub(&mut self) -> Result<(), CalcError>` in `src/lib.rs`. push: self.stack.push(value). pop: self.stack.pop().ok_or(CalcError::StackUnderflow). add: pop two values b and a, push a+b. sub: pop b and a, push a-b. Run `cargo test --quiet`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `mul()` (a*b) and `div()` (a/b with DivisionByZero error when b==0). Run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any failures.
Final step: implement `dup()` — peek at the top value and push a copy — and `swap()` — pop two values and push them back in swapped order. Run `cargo test --quiet` — all 6 tests must pass.
success_criteria: push/pop work; pop returns StackUnderflow when empty
add/sub pop two operands and push result
mul/div work; div returns DivisionByZero when divisor is 0
